 The Hon'Ble Mr Justice P. Vadamalai

 Anusuya 
 Vs.
 Nagendran 
 Prayer : Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is filed under Secti
 the Code of Civil Procedure, to withdraw the proceeding in H.M.O.P.
 No.351 of 2024 on the file of the Family Court, Thanjavur and trans
 same to the file of the Family Court, Dindigul.

For Petitioner : Mr.P.Thirumahilmaran
 For Respondent : Mr.A.Sivanu Pandian
 Order

The present Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition has been filed to withdraw the proceeding in H.M.O.P.No.351 of 2024 on the file of the Family Court, Thanjavur and transfer the same to the file of the Family Court, Dindigul.

Page No 1 of 5 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 20/03/2025 06:19:54 pm )
2.
The petitioner is the wife and the respondent is the husband.
The marriage between the petitioner and the respondent was solemnized on 27.01.2023 at New Sabaiyar Mahal, Thanjavur as per the Hindu Rites and Customs.
Out of wedlock, no child was born.

3. Due to disputes and differences, the parties have separated, and the respondent/husband has initiated the proceeding in H.M.O.P.No.351 of 2024 on the file of the Family Court, Thanjavur seeking divorce.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondent.

sentences.text: 5. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner/wife is now residing at Kannuvarankottai, Dindigul District under the care of her parents.

The distance between Kannuvarankottai and Thanjavur is around 400 Kms to and fro, and the petitioner/wife, being a lady, finds it very difficult to travel such a long distance for attending every Court hearing.

Hence,
she seeks transfer of proceeding in H.M.O.P.No.351 of 2024 from the file of the Family Court,
Thanjavur to the file of the Family Court, Dindigul.
Page No 2 of 5 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 20/03/2025 06:19:54 pm )

6. The learned counsel for the respondent would submit that when the respondent/husband returned to India to attend his father's funeral, the petitioner/wife, along with her parents and brother, threatened the respondent by demanding him not to go to abroad again.

Further, he would submit that on the third day after the death of the respondent's father, the respondent was arrested by the police, because of the false complaint lodged by the petitioner under Dowry Prohibition Act and Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.

Thereafter, the petitioner was taken to the police station,
and he was kept there overnight.
Hence, the learned counsel for the respondent has raised strong objection to allow this petition.

7. However, it is well settled proposition of law that whenever the transfer petition is filed in matrimonial disputes, the convenience of the wife should be predominantly looked into, and the wifes convenience shall be given preference.
8. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, and also considering the convenience of the wife, this Court is inclined to allow this petition.

Page No 3 of 5 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 20/03/2025 06:19:54 pm )
9.

The learned Judge, Family Court, Thanjavur is directed to transmit the entire records pertaining to the case, in H.M.O.P.No.351 of 2024, to the file of the Family Court, Dindigul within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, and on receipt of such records, the learned Judge, Family Court, Dindigul is directed to take the case on file and dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law.
10. Accordingly, this Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition stands allowed.
No costs.

Consequently,
the connected Civil Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
